pages.title: Leading the charge to make health care accessible to all - Diana DeGette
pages.text:
## Leading the charge to make health care accessible to all
Access to health care has been a long time struggle for many Americans. Diana has made it a priority to fight for expanding health care access, securing funding for medical research, supporting medical professionals and patient protections. She played a crucial role in the passage of the Affordable Care Act and has been a leader in the U.S. House on health insurance protocols.
Most recently, Diana co-authored the 21st Century Cures Act, which modernizes the National Institutes of Health and processes for key medical research. The 21st Century Cures Act included funding for Vice President Joe Biden’s Cancer Moonshot, securing the funds needed to accelerate cancer research.
## Protecting and improving consumers across the country

pages.title: Protecting natural resources and combating climate change - Diana DeGette
pages.text:
## Protecting natural resources and combating climate change
Threats to our natural resources and our environment are cause for serious concern in Colorado and across the country. Diana is a leading voice on environmental issues in Congress and is working to protect both Colorado’s public lands and our global environment. She’s the author of the landmark Colorado Wilderness Act, which would protect and preserve 1.6 million acres of pristine land across Colorado for generations to come.
## Leading the charge to make health care accessible to all

pages.title: Fighting for women’s ability to make health care choices - Diana DeGette
pages.text:
## Fighting for women’s ability to make health care choices
As the co-chair of the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus, Diana has fought for common-sense family planning and reproductive rights. At a time when women’s health care is under constant attack, Diana has spearheaded efforts to protect funding for Planned Parenthood, include access to birth control and comprehensive reproductive health care in health care legislation and leads her caucus in setting a pro-choice agenda.
## Protecting natural resources and combating climate change

pages.title: Protecting and improving consumers across the country - Diana DeGette
pages.text:
## Protecting and improving consumers across the country
Diana has taken a leading role in advocating for the protection of our nation’s food supply. Diana believes that the protection of our nation’s food supply should be recognized as a critical component of our national security. She is the author of two key pieces of legislation that go a long way toward securing our nation’s food supply.
SAFER (Safe And Fair Enforcement & Recall) Food Act, would give the United States Department of Agriculture and the Food and Drug Administration the authority to force a recall of all contaminated foods.
The TRACE (Tracing and Recalling Agricultural Contamination) Act would authorize the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a product tracing system to track products from their origins to the grocery store, enabling faster recall in the event of contamination.
Both food safety measures were endorsed by the New York Times and The Washington Post, and continue to be lauded by newspapers across the country.
Diana was also a key player in the creation and passage of groundbreaking consumer product safety legislation that was signed into law in 2008.
## Fighting for women’s ability to make health care choices

February 9, 2021 Media
## Space Ref: Lawmakers Introduce Bipartisan Plan to Provide U.S. Researchers $25 Billion in Emergency Funding
Last Friday, a bipartisan group of lawmakers – led by U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette (D-CO) – introduced legislation to provide billions of dollars in emergency relief to U.S. researchers to continue their important, federally-funded projects through the pandemic.
The legislation – known as the Research Investment to Spark the Economy, or RISE, Act – would provide $25 billion to independent research institutions, public laboratories and universities throughout the country to continue their work on thousands of federally-backed projects.
It comes as tens of thousands of researchers – including graduate students, postdocs and technical support staff – find themselves at risk of losing their jobs – and their work – as universities and independent research institutions look to cut costs as a result of the ongoing pandemic.
“America has some of the best and brightest minds in the world working on potentially groundbreaking research,” DeGette said. “We can’t afford to lose them or their important work. Ensuring our researchers have the resources they need to continue finding innovative solutions to some of our nation’s toughest problems is vital to our national security and our ability to remain competitive on the world stage. Any lapse in funding now could set us back years, possibly even decades.”
While significant investments have been made to fund new research centered around addressing the ongoing COVID-19 crisis, many other federally-funded projects are now at risk of being stalled, delayed or even shuttered.
The legislation introduced today would provide the nation’s science-related agencies – such as the U.S. Depts. of Health and Human Services, Agriculture, Energy, the Environmental Protection Agency and the National Science Foundation – an additional $25 billion to award to various universities and research institutions to continue their work on ongoing federally-funded projects.
The funding could also be used by these institutions to keep researchers involved in a recent federally-funded project on staff for up to two years, to prevent them from having to find work elsewhere, potentially outside the United States.
In addition to DeGette, the legislation is cosponsored U.S. Reps. Fred Upton (R-MI), Eddie Bernice Johnson (D-TX), Anna Eshoo (D-CA), Anthony Gonzalez (R-OH) and 73 other members of Congress. It also has the support of more than 320 higher education, research and industry groups – including Google, U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Association of American Universities.
“I am deeply concerned that due to the COVID-19 pandemic, a number of American research institutions may not survive, years of important research will be lost, and we will suffer irreparable harm to our talent pipeline,” said Johnson. “We cannot allow that long-term damage to happen—the stakes are far too high. For those reasons, I did not hesitate to join my bipartisan colleagues in cosponsoring the RISE Act again this Congress.”
“The COVID-19 pandemic has wreaked havoc on all segments of society, including America’s preeminent research institutions that conduct cutting edge breakthroughs and lead in global innovation,” Eshoo said. “Much of that groundbreaking research has come to a halt due to COVID safety measures imposed by local governments and it’s why there’s a need for emergency funding. The RISE Act will breathe new life into federally-funded research and enable our nation’s brilliant researchers to continue their critical work.”
“In the past year we have seen how valuable science, research, and innovation are to our nation’s public health, national security, economic growth and international competitiveness,” Upton said. “The RISE Act is critical legislation that will support our researchers at Western Michigan University and universities across the country. Preserving our innovation pipeline will help ensure America remains a global leader in research and development.”
“For nearly a year, Americans have been battling the devastating impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic physically, mentally, and financially,” said Gonzalez. “Many working in our country’s research enterprise are now at risk of losing their jobs due to lack of funding. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the RISE Act, which will authorize vital funds for emergency relief to support America’s research enterprise.”
DeGette introduced a similar version of the legislation last year that was included in the HEREOS Act Congress passed in September, providing researchers with $7.6 billion in emergency relief. The legislation introduced today would provide researchers an additional $25 billion on top of that.

pages.title: Issues - Diana DeGette
pages.text:
Dedicated. Passionate. Working for you.
## Diana's Priorities
Diana’s priorities in Colorado and in the U.S. House
Diana’s proud to be able to work for Colorado’s 1st Congressional District. Learn more about what she is focused on delivering for Colorado and our country as she represents CO-01 in the U.S. House.
Diana is standing up to Trump to defend our democracy, protect our rights, and restore the American Dream. After the January 6th attacks, she served as an impeachment manager to hold Trump accountable. Now she is leading the fight against his unconstitutional war in Iran and his abuses of power both at home and abroad.
## Challenging Unconstitutional Actions
- Helping lead legal challenges to strike down unlawful executive orders
- Fighting attempts to gut federal programs Colorado depends on
- Defending birthright citizenship and the 14th Amendment
- Protecting due process against executive overreach
## Defending Vulnerable Communities
- Calling out attacks on the LGBTQ community
- Condemning anti-immigrant policies that target families, separate parents from their kids, and criminalize asylum seekers
- Publicly defending those unjustly targeted by the administration
## Restoring Sanity to Our Government
- Calling for hearings and investigations into the politicization of federal agencies under Trump appointees
- Fighting for transparency and opposing the purge of inspectors general across more than a dozen federal agencies — watchdogs who root out fraud, waste, and abuse regardless of who is in power
- Fighting against political retaliation and mass firings of the civil servants who deliver Social Security checks, process veterans’ benefits, and keep food and medicine safe
- Demanding accountability at Trump’s Department of Justice, including for the firing of career prosecutors and the use of federal law enforcement to target political opponents
Diana is standing up to ICE abuses because she believes our immigration system must reflect dignity, fairness, and humanity — never cruelty or fear. She is fighting to keep families together, protect workers, and create a real path to citizenship.
## Holding ICE Accountable
- Calling for abolishing ICE, an agency that has lost the trust of the communities it operates in
- Pushing to ban federal agents from wearing masks and rein in their out-of-control behavior as a cosponsor of the No Secret Police Act
- Voted against creating the Department of Homeland Security, warning it could lead to a domestic police force without proper oversight or accountability
- Conducted an inspection of the ICE detention facility in Aurora to demand better treatment of detainees and transparency in how their cases are handled
- Introduced a plan to grant lawful status to Denver immigrant rights leader Jeanette Vizguerra, detained by ICE while working her job at a Target
## Fighting for a Humane Immigration System
- Championing comprehensive immigration reform that includes a real path to citizenship
- Defending Dreamers and pushing to pass the DREAM Act to give certainty for immigrants brought here as children
- Standing up to Trump’s effort to shut the door on asylum seekers and advocating for a strong Refugee Admissions Program that reflects American values
## Exposing Trump’s Cruelty
- Chaired the first congressional oversight hearings on Trump’s family separation policy, forcing administration officials to answer for tearing children from their parents
- Speaking out against ICE raids that target families, separate parents from their kids, and criminalize people seeking asylum
- Demanding due process for immigrants picked up by ICE without warning or legal justification
Diana has secured tens of millions of dollars in federal funding for affordable housing, food access, health care, and other critical services in Denver. Her work has delivered real, tangible results for working families across the city.
## Expanding Affordable Housing and Tackling Homelessness
- Secured $4 million for Warren Village to construct 74 apartments for low-income single-parent families in southwest Denver
- Directed $4 million to the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless to convert under-utilized hotels into housing for people experiencing homelessness
- Secured $3 million for Urban Peak to construct a new shelter for homeless youth
- Directed $2 million to the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless to build a new recuperative care facility for people with serious medical and behavioral health needs
- Secured $1.4 million for the City and County of Denver’s FreshLo Project, bringing 97 units of affordable housing to Montbello
- Secured $1 million for Habitat for Humanity of Metro Denver to help build six new single-family homes in Villa Park
## Fighting Hunger and Building Food Security
- Secured $1.2 million for the Food Bank of the Rockies’ Montbello headquarters to expand food storage and distribution for thousands of Denver families
- Directed $800,000 to Re:Vision to help create an urban farm in Westwood, strengthening neighborhood food security
- Secured $750,000 for We Don’t Waste to grow food recovery efforts across Denver
## Expanding Access to Health Care and Community Services
- Secured $2 million to expand Tepeyac Community Health Center’s facility on East 48th Street
- Directed $2 million to Servicios de La Raza to build a community center serving low-income residents in Barnum
- Secured $1 million for the Center for African American Health’s Hudson Street building renovation to add mental health offices, a tech room, and job readiness space
Diana DeGette believes health care is a human right, not a privilege. She has long championed universal coverage to ensure every American can access high-quality, affordable care.
## Pass Medicare for All
- An original co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act
- Would guarantee every American can see a doctor, fill a prescription, and get the care they need regardless of income or employment
- As the top Democrat on the powerful Health Subcommittee, Diana will be best positioned to build the coalition to pass this landmark legislation
## Standing Up to RFK Jr. and Anti-Science Extremists
- Grilled RFK Jr. on the firing of leading medical researchers, replacement of vaccine experts with anti-vaxxers, and exposed his ignorance about the cuts gutting his own department
- Demanded RFK Jr. answer for his careless cuts and assure the public that science, not conspiracy theories, would guide HHS decisions
- Authored the bipartisan 21st Century Cures Act to speed lifesaving treatments to patients and accelerate research into cancer, Alzheimer’s, and rare diseases
## Fighting Cuts to Medicaid and Other Essential Health Care
- Opposing Republican cuts to Medicaid that would rip coverage from more than 1.4 million Coloradans, including children, seniors, people with disabilities, and working families
- Standing up against partisan efforts to defund Planned Parenthood and block patients from accessing reproductive and primary care
- Defending the Affordable Care Act against repeal attempts and fighting to protect coverage for people with pre-existing conditions
## Lowering Drug Costs and Improving Health Outcomes
- Helped pass the law capping out-of-pocket prescription drug costs at $2,000 a year for seniors on Medicare, saving 11 million enrollees billions in annual costs
- As Co-Chair of the Diabetes Caucus, championed efforts to make insulin affordable and voted to cap insulin costs at $35 a month
- Co-authored the Preventing Maternal Deaths Act to strengthen efforts to investigate and prevent pregnancy-related deaths
- Pushing to extend the $35 insulin cap and the $2,000 prescription drug cap to every American, not just those on Medicare
As Co-Chair of the Reproductive Freedom Caucus, Diana DeGette is one of Congress’s most steadfast champions for our reproductive rights. She believes every person should have the freedom to make their own decisions about their body, their health, and their future.
## A National Leader for Abortion Rights
- Leading the fight in Congress to restore the protections of Roe v. Wade nationwide
- Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Action Fund and Reproductive Freedom for All (formerly NARAL), the two largest reproductive freedom organizations in the country
- Leading champion of the Women’s Health Protection Act, the landmark bill to codify the right to abortion into federal law
- Co-author of the EACH Act to overturn the Hyde Amendment, the decades-old ban that denies abortion coverage to millions of low-income Americans on Medicaid
## Defending Against Partisan Attacks
- Defending Planned Parenthood and Title X providers against Republican defunding efforts
- Protecting access to medication abortion from Trump’s attacks, leading more than 250 members of Congress in an effort to protect this safe and effective treatment at the Supreme Court
- Shielding abortion providers from retaliatory, out-of-state attacks through the Let Doctors Provide Reproductive Health Care Act
## Expanding Access to Contraception and Basic Care
- Earned a 100% rating from Reproductive Freedom for All for her voting record on protecting and expanding abortion access, contraception, and reproductive health care
- Original co-sponsor of the Right to Contraception Act to guarantee every American the right to access birth control and family planning services
- Led the successful effort to stop the Trump administration from allowing employers to strip birth control coverage from their employees
- Author of Colorado’s “Bubble Bill” protecting patients and providers from harassment at reproductive health clinics, a law upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court
Diana believes every family deserves the freedom to build a stable life without being crushed by rising costs. That’s why she’s fighting to bring down the cost of groceries, housing, prescriptions, and care — and to build an economy where Denverites can afford to live in the city we all love.
## Lowering Costs for Colorado Families
- Voted to end Trump’s tariffs, a hidden tax that has raised prices on groceries, cars, lumber, and household goods
- Working to prevent future presidents from imposing these dangerous tariffs without Congressional approval
- Expanding affordable housing, access to child care, and reducing energy bills
## Bringing Down the Cost of Health Care
- Original co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act, guaranteeing every American can see a doctor and fill a prescription regardless of income or employment
- Helped pass the law capping out-of-pocket prescription drug costs at $2,000 a year for seniors on Medicare
- Fighting Republican cuts to Medicaid that would rip coverage from more than 1 million Coloradans
- Defending the Affordable Care Act against Republican attacks and protecting coverage for people with pre-existing conditions, especially young children
## Building a Fair Economy
- Defending Social Security and Medicare against Republican efforts to cut benefits, raise the retirement age, or hand them over to Wall Street
- Original co-sponsor of the Raise the Wage Act to lift the federal minimum wage and give 22 million Americans a long-overdue raise
- Co-sponsor of the PRO Act to protect the right to organize, hold lawbreaking employers accountable, and strengthen workers’ power at the bargaining table
- Endorsed by the Colorado AFL-CIO, SEIU Colorado, and other local unions for her record of standing with working men and women
Diana is one of Congress’s strongest voices for protecting our environment. She believes every community deserves clean air, clean water, and a healthy planet — and she has led major national efforts to safeguard Colorado’s natural resources and confront the climate crisis head-on.
## Cutting Pollution and Tackling Climate Change
- Wrote the first federal clean electricity standard to move the country to 100% zero-emission electricity by 2050 — or sooner
- Authored the law to crack down on methane pollution, one of the most potent contributors to climate change — methane emissions particularly affect frontline communities when leaked from oil and gas refineries like Suncor just outside Denver
- Working to stop the Trump administration from gutting EPA rules that limit air and water pollution
- Fighting to protect vital clean energy investments from Republican budget cuts
## Protecting Colorado’s Public Lands
- Author of the Colorado Wilderness Act to permanently protect more than 720,000 acres of wilderness in Colorado
- Pushing back against the Trump administration’s sell-off of public lands to oil, gas, and mining companies
- Defending Colorado’s outdoor recreation economy, which supports 511,000 jobs and generates $37 billion in annual consumer spending
## Advancing Environmental Justice
- Author of the plan to require the EPA to identify and clean up 100 of the most heavily polluted communities in the country
- Fighting for Globeville, Elyria-Swansea, and other north Denver neighborhoods that have lived for decades with the cumulative health burden of nearby highways, rail yards, and industrial facilities
- Pushing the EPA to assess how multiple sources of pollution can affect community health — something current federal rules fail to require

## CBS4 Denver: Rep. Diana DeGette Plans To Create National Clean Energy Standard
DENVER (CBS4)– Colorado Congresswoman Diana DeGette plans to create the first national clean energy standard. The Democrat represents Colorado’s 1st Congressional District in Washington, DC.
DeGette is introducing a bill that would require all utilities to cut carbon emissions in half by 2030 and to net-zero by 2050.
“I vetted it with everybody, environmental groups like it, power companies like it, state local governments like it, because it really gives us a path to how we can get to those goals,” said DeGette.
The bill would require energy producers to earn a certain number of clean energy credits each year for reducing the amount of electricity they produce or face penalties.
DeGette said she is still looking for a Republican sponsor.

## Colorado Politics: DeGette announces COVID-19 oversight agenda
U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette, who chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, announced on Tuesday that her agenda for investigating the Trump Administration’s response to COVID-19 includes reviews of equipment supply chains, vaccine development and testing efforts.
Calling the administration’s coronavirus response “inconsistent and inadequate,” DeGette and committee chair U.S. Rep. Frank Pallone, D-N.J., said in a joint statement that the oversight plan “focuses on some of the key areas where the administration has failed the American people, the states and marginalized communities. “
DeGette’s subcommittee will continue to prompt the administration for its plan to increase diagnostic and antibody testing, as well as monitor the federal government’s ability to support contact tracing and monitor infection trends.
Members will also investigate the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s interaction with the personal protective equipment supply chain, and whether the agency is “playing a more proactive role in decisions related to distribution of supplies.” Earlier this month, after Gov. Jared Polis accused FEMA of delaying state orders of ventilators to fulfill their own needs, a spokesperson responded that “FEMA has not and is not seizing or taking supplies or personal protective equipment.”
Vaccine production, the safety of food workers, and the administration’s ability to “prioritize the public interest” are the final items on the subcommittee’s agenda. DeGette cited President Donald Trump’s decision to defund the World Health Organization, his dismissal of multiple inspectors general, and a ban on fetal tissue in COVID-19 research as actions that called into question for her the White House’s dedication to public health.

## Colorado Politics: DeGette requests timeline for Trump Administration’s vaccination plan
U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette has requested that the White House Coronavirus Task Force and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services say when they plan to release a national plan for vaccinating the U.S. populace against COVID-19.
“In our letter, we requested critical information about the Administration’s vaccine planning efforts and sought a copy of the plan itself,” wrote DeGette, referring to a communication that she and U.S. Rep. Frank Pallone, Jr., D-N.J., sent to the White House in May. “More than two months later, we have yet to receive a response. According to testimony from senior Administration officials before this Committee on June 23, and before the Senate Committee on Appropriations on July 2, such a plan is still under development more than six months into the COVID-19 pandemic.”
Pallone chairs the U.S. House Committee on Energy and Commerce, and DeGette heads the oversight and investigations subcommittee. In their latest letter dated Aug. 5, the lawmakers asked to know about the planned involvement of the U.S. Department of Defense in distributing a vaccine and of and various health organizations in developing guidelines.
“Despite the lack of a comprehensive plan, the White House and the Operation Warp Speed (OWS) initiative appear to be advancing decisions that will impact future COVID-19 vaccine distribution efforts,” DeGette and Pallone wrote. “In an interview on May 14, 2020, President Trump indicated that the U.S. military would be mobilized to distribute a COVID-19 vaccine once it was available.”
They continued by expressing concern that “ongoing efforts do not appear to fully incorporate CDC, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), and state, territorial, tribal, and local health departments, all of which have played critical roles in planning and implementing existing vaccine programs and prior outbreak responses.”
According to a fact sheet released by the White House on July 27, the nation is “seeing tremendous progress” on the vaccine-development strategy, but there was no mention of a distribution plan.
